findings.summary: The whole SubscriptionHub half of this commit can be reverted with both new tests green: the key reaches the log through MemoryBinStore's own IOException text, not through the production message. MEASURED.
findings.detail:
SURVIVING MUTATION, run in a throwaway worktree with the staged diff applied: replace `throw new UncheckedIOException("segment " + segmentKey + " could not be read for delivery", storeFailed)` (SubscriptionHub.java:388-389, the entire second production hunk) with the pre-change `throw new UncheckedIOException(storeFailed)`. `./gradlew :ingest:test --tests '*UndeliverablePushTest*' --tests '*DefaultIngestTest*'` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 22s, no `error:` in the log.

WHY IT SURVIVES: `UncheckedIOException(IOException)` sets its message to `cause.toString()`, and the fake backend throws `new IOException("no such key: " + key)` (binstore-backends/.../MemoryBinStore.java:49). So `e.getMessage()` in `DefaultIngest.pushLoop`'s WARNING contains `seg-no-pod-ever-wrote-this` EITHER WAY, and the only assertion on the line -- `.contains("seg-no-pod-ever-wrote-this")` at :132 -- cannot tell the two apart.

WHAT THAT MEANS IN PRODUCTION: the commit's stated reason for touching `deliver` is that it is 'the last frame that knows' the failing key. A real backend fails with `Connection reset`, `Access Denied`, `Read timed out` -- none of which name the object -- and the reverted form then logs a line with NO failing key, which is exactly the defect the row says review caught (`next.segmentKey()` naming a healthy object). The test would stay green through that regression, and through any future edit that drops the key from the hub message, because the assertion is satisfied by the fake's text.

KILL: drive the failure with a store whose IOException does NOT name the key -- ingest/src/test/java/binjava/ingest/StoreFakes.java already hosts that family (`FailingPuts`, `FailWritesOnCommand`) -- so `contains(key)` can only be satisfied by the message `deliver` constructs. A direct T0/T1 case on `SubscriptionHub.deliver` asserting `UncheckedIOException.getMessage()` names the key would be cheaper still and pins the production seam where it lives rather than three frames up.
findings.failure_scenario: Mutation (measured, BUILD SUCCESSFUL): SubscriptionHub.java:388 `throw new UncheckedIOException("segment " + segmentKey + " could not be read for delivery", storeFailed)` -> `throw new UncheckedIOException(storeFailed)`. Both new tests and DefaultIngestTest stay green, because UncheckedIOException(IOException) uses cause.toString() and MemoryBinStore:49 throws `new IOException("no such key: " + key)` -- the key in the log comes from the fake, not from the code under test. Under a backend whose IOException does not name the object (S3 'Connection reset'/'Access Denied'), the reverted code logs no failing key at all and the suite never notices.

findings.summary: The log LEVEL is unconstrained: demoting the line from WARNING to TRACE leaves both tests green, and a TRACE line is invisible under every default JUL configuration -- the silence this task exists to end.
findings.detail:
SURVIVING MUTATION, measured in the same worktree: `LOG.log(System.Logger.Level.WARNING, ...)` -> `LOG.log(System.Logger.Level.TRACE, ...)` at DefaultIngest.java:403. `./gradlew :ingest:test --tests '*UndeliverablePushTest*' --tests '*DefaultIngestTest*'` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 21s, no `error:`.

WHY IT SURVIVES: the probe sets itself to `Level.ALL` (:113) AND raises the ROOT logger to `Level.ALL` (:119), so every level from TRACE up reaches it; the assertion then reads only `record.getMessage()` and never `record.getLevel()`. The task's deliverable is 'a WARNING line beside the increment'; at TRACE (JUL FINER) the line is dropped by the default root level of INFO in any deployment, so an operator gets a counter that rose and no way to learn WHICH segment -- the counter alone being the exact state the row calls unactionable.

KILL, one of two, both one line: (a) capture the LogRecord and assert `record.getLevel()` is at least `Level.WARNING`; or (b) simply do not raise the root level -- a WARNING record passes the default INFO root level and reaches the handler unaided, while a demoted line is filtered and the assertion reds. (b) also removes the global-state mutation and the `realLevel` restore entirely.

(State restoration itself is correct: `removeHandler` + `setLevel(realLevel)` are in a `finally` that runs even if `close()` throws, and no JUnit parallel execution is configured in this repo, so the global mutation does not leak into a concurrent test.)
findings.failure_scenario: Mutation (measured, BUILD SUCCESSFUL): DefaultIngest.java:403 `System.Logger.Level.WARNING` -> `System.Logger.Level.TRACE`. theWarningNamesTheSegmentThatCouldNotBeREAD still passes because the test raises both the probe handler and the ROOT logger to Level.ALL (:113, :119) and asserts only on record.getMessage(). In production at the default root level of INFO the line never appears, so the operator sees a counter rise with no segment named.
